Exact wording TBD". Hard-coded into template/theme files — do not finalise until wording confirmed |

For international storefronts (HK, ME, US Intl, EU Intl): Global-e handles product pricing — do not render SFCC prices for international until Global-e pricing flow is confirmed (see [regional.md](regional.md) and [checkout.md](checkout.md) section 14) |

A colour swatch is just the UI element, but whether clicking it loads a new style code hinges on the data model — if each colour is a separate product (Model B), you get a new URL and full reload; if it's a variation (Model A), you stay on the same page with JS swapping the details. Model A is cheaper and smoother UX-wise but requires the catalogue to structure colours as variants on a master product, whereas Model B treats each colour as its own product with its own identity.

There's a third path worth considering: keep colours as separate products but use client-side navigation instead of a hard reload, so the URL and style code change without the browser refreshing the whole page. That could satisfy both bullets — new style code and new URL, but with the perceived performance and UX benefits of a soft transition.

Looking back at the PRD, there's something important: PRD-062 explicitly states the gallery updates when a colour swatch is selected without a full page reload. There's a tension here between what the PRD says should happen and what the reference example shows.

The real issue is that SFCC-91's acceptance criteria calls for "new style code + full reload" (Model B), while PRD-062 says no reload (Model A). Good question — the two AC bullets aren't just worded differently, they describe **two different catalogue data models**, and "style code" is the tell.

**Quick definitions**
- **Colour swatch** = the UI element (the clickable thumbnail for each colour).
- **Style code** = the product's *identity* in SFCC (the SKU / product ID that the PDP URL resolves to).

The question the AC never settles: **when you click another colour, are you staying on the same product or navigating to a different one?** That depends on how colours are modelled.

| | **Model A — colour as a variation** | **Model B — colour as its own product** |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC structure | One master product; colour + size are variation attributes | Each colour is a **separate product with its own style code** |
| Clicking a swatch | Swaps the variant *within the same product* | **Navigates to a different product page** |
| URL | Same page, e.g. `?color=lilac` | New URL, e.g. `…/lumi-sandal-lilac` → `…/lumi-sandal-black` |
| Style code | Unchanged | **Changes** (new SKU) |
| Reload | **No reload** (JS swap) | New product load |
| Maps to AC bullet | "Colour variation… **without full page reload**" | "**New Style Code**… full page reload" |
| Build | OOTB base `swatch-group` — cheap (~3) | Custom: colour-group + sibling links + navigation (~5–8 + spike) |
| SEO | One URL for all colours | Each colour independently indexable (better) |

So they're the same click producing **opposite outcomes** — that's the contradiction. It can't be both; the team has to pick the model.

**Which is real?** The live site points to **Model B** — each colour is its own URL (`lumi-sandal-lilac.html`), and that usually mirrors the AP21/ERP reality where each colourway is a distinct style code. That's also why the base `swatch-group` won't work as-is and why I flagged the estimate risk.

**But there's a PRD tension too:** `pdp.md` **PRD-062 (confirmed)** says *"gallery updates … when a colour swatch is selected, **without a full page reload**"* — i.e. Model A behaviour, contradicting the "new style code + reload" bullet.

**Likely reconciliation to propose in the room:** colours *are* separate products/style codes (Model B), but the swatch does a **client-side (SPA) route change** — new URL + new style code, but **no hard browser reload**. That satisfies PRD-062's "no reload," keeps SEO-friendly per-colour URLs, and protects the LCP budget. If that's the intent, the AC should be rewritten as one bullet, not two.

**Ask:** "Are colourways separate style codes or variation attributes — and if separate, do we want a hard reload or a soft client-side transition?" That one answer resolves the AC *and* locks the estimate.
